phys-mech-01-c3.text: NASA Glenn Research Center. Newton's Laws of Motion. NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics.
phys-mech-01-c3.quote: Whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.
phys-mech-01-c3.claim: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

phys-mech-01-c1.text: NASA Glenn Research Center. Newton's Laws of Motion. NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics.
phys-mech-01-c1.quote: If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.
phys-mech-01-c1.claim: An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion at constant velocity, unless acted on by a net external force.

phys-mech-02-c1.text: R. Nave. Kinetic Energy. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-02-c1.quote: Kinetic energy is energy of motion. The SI unit for energy is the joule = newton x meter in accordance with the basic definition of energy as the capacity for doing work.
phys-mech-02-c1.claim: Kinetic energy is energy of motion

phys-mech-02-c2.text: R. Nave. Kinetic Energy. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-02-c2.quote: The total energy of an isolated system is subject to the conservation of energy principle.
phys-mech-02-c2.claim: In a closed system, total energy is conserved

phys-mech-03-c2.text: R. Nave. Friction. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-03-c2.quote: the amount of force required to move an object starting from rest is usually greater than the force required to keep it moving at constant velocity once it is started.
phys-mech-03-c2.claim: it's harder to start pushing a heavy box than to keep it sliding

phys-mech-03-c2.text: R. Nave. Friction. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-03-c2.quote: Frictional resistance to the relative motion of two solid objects is usually proportional to the force which presses the surfaces together as well as the roughness of the surfaces.
phys-mech-03-c2.claim: Both depend on the normal force and a coefficient of friction

phys-mech-04-c1.text: R. Nave. Centripetal Force. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-04-c1.quote: Any motion in a curved path represents accelerated motion, and requires a force directed toward the center of curvature of the path.
phys-mech-04-c1.claim: An object moving in a circle is constantly changing direction

phys-mech-04-c1.text: R. Nave. Centripetal Force. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-04-c1.quote: Swinging a mass on a string requires string tension, and the mass will travel off in a tangential straight line if the string breaks.
phys-mech-04-c1.claim: For a ball on a string, tension provides it.

phys-mech-04-c2.text: R. Nave. Torque and Equilibrium. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-04-c2.quote: A torque is an influence which tends to change the rotational motion of an object.
phys-mech-04-c2.claim: Torque is what changes rotational motion, just as force changes linear motion.

phys-mech-04-c3.text: R. Nave. Moment of Inertia: Rotational-Linear Parallels. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-04-c3.quote: If the string is pulled down so that the radius is half the original radius, then conservation of angular momentum dictates that the ball must have four times the angular velocity.
phys-mech-04-c3.claim: pulling arms in (mass closer to axis) makes them spin faster: angular momentum is conserved

phys-mech-05-c1.text: D. P. Stern. Newton and the Law of Gravitation. From Stargazers to Starships, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center.
phys-mech-05-c1.quote: Newton showed that if gravity at a distance R was proportional to 1 / R2 (varied like the " inverse square of the distance "), then indeed the acceleration g measured at the Earth's surface would correctly predict the orbital period T of the Moon.
phys-mech-05-c1.claim: Newton realized that the same force that pulls an apple to the ground holds the Moon in orbit.

phys-mech-05-c1.text: R. Nave. Gravity. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-05-c1.quote: The gravitational force between two masses m1 and m2 is given by the relationship: This is often called the "universal law of gravitation" and G the universal gravitation constant. It is an example of an inverse square law force.
phys-mech-05-c1.claim: Every mass attracts every other mass with a force

phys-mech-05-c3.text: R. Nave. Kepler's Laws. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-05-c3.quote: All planets move in elliptical orbits, with the sun at one focus.
phys-mech-05-c3.claim: Orbits are ellipses, with the Sun at one focus, not perfect circles.

phys-mech-05-c3.text: NASA. Orbits and Kepler's Laws. NASA Science.
phys-mech-05-c3.quote: Kepler's Second Law: the imaginary line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps equal areas of space during equal time intervals as the planet orbits.
phys-mech-05-c3.claim: Equal areas in equal times: planets move faster when closer to the Sun.

phys-mech-06-c2.text: R. Nave. Trajectories. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-06-c2.quote: The launch at 45 degrees gives the maximum range.

phys-mech-06-c1.text: R. Nave. Trajectories. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-06-c1.quote: The horizontal and vertical motions may be separated and described by the general motion equations for constant acceleration.
phys-mech-06-c1.claim: This decomposition turns a complicated 2D problem into two independent 1D problems.

phys-mech-06-c3.text: R. Nave. Air Friction. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-06-c3.quote: For higher velocites and larger objects the frictional drag is approximately proportional to the square of the velocity
phys-mech-06-c3.claim: Air drag scales roughly as v² for fast objects (baseballs, missiles)

phys-mech-07-c1.text: R. Nave. Center of Mass. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-07-c1.quote: The concept of the center of mass is that of an average of the masses factored by their distances from a reference point.
phys-mech-07-c1.claim: The center of mass of an extended object is the weighted-average position of all its mass elements.

phys-mech-07-c1.text: R. Nave. Center of Mass. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-mech-07-c1.quote: the unique point in an object or system which can be used to describe the system's response to external forces and torques.
phys-mech-07-c1.claim: For external forces, an extended body behaves as if all its mass were concentrated at the center of mass.

phys-mech-08-c3.text: C. Blair. Noether's Theorem (lecture notes). Trinity College Dublin, School of Mathematics.
phys-mech-08-c3.quote: Note also what the theorem essentially means is that for every continuous symmetry there corresponds a conserved quantity
phys-mech-08-c3.claim: every continuous symmetry of the Lagrangian gives a conserved quantity

phys-mech-08-c3.text: K. Intriligator (2011). Lecture 14: Noether's theorem. UC San Diego Physics.
phys-mech-08-c3.quote: Gives conserved quantity ~n · P~ , where P~ is the total momentum. Conservation of total momentum.
